frequency_question: How often do central banks implement incremental reserve ratio measures within a designated four-month window given observable systemic liquidity precursors?
membership_rule: Members are formal policy announcements of incremental, temporary, or ad-hoc cash reserve ratio hikes targeting specific systemic excess liquidity pools by major emerging market central banks (e.g., RBI, Bank of Indonesia, PBOC) since 2004. Excluded are standard, scheduled changes to headline reserve requirement ratios.
window: Any four-month calendar window during an active monetary tightening or excess liquidity sterilization cycle.

cases.name: RBI Incremental CRR historic episodes (implied sub-cases)
PBoC Reserve Requirement Ratio targeted frequency subset

provenance_note: claims 18 cases from only 3 named (6.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 3 named/structured instances; estimated roughly 18 relevant comparative windows globally over 20 years.
known_gaps: Exact internal deliberations of central bank boards regarding the choice between variable rate reverse repos (VRRR) versus iCRR are opaque, leading to potential undercounting of near-misses.
skeleton: Liquidity sterilization cycles in major emerging market central banks over the past two decades, broken down by distinct liquidity surge episodes (approx. 6 major cycles), with an average duration of 3 years each, yielding approximately 36 four-month windows per cycle across major jurisdictions, of which targeted incremental ratio deployments occurred in a specific subset of windows characterized by sudden liquidity shocks.
multiplier: 6 cycles x 3 targeted intervention windows per cycle = 18 total historical windows where precursor liquidity conditions matched, with 4 resulting in actual iCRR or equivalent direct incremental ratio announcements.
validity_reason: Central bank liquidity management toolkits evolve slowly over multi-year structural regime changes; the current preference for hybrid liquidity management remains stable through the medium term.
